tagline: Up the Delaware, the old canal between road and river.
intro: Route 29 comes out of a tunnel on the Trenton riverbank and heads north with the Delaware close by. Past the Scudder Falls Bridge it becomes a two-lane River Road, and from there the Delaware and Raritan feeder canal mostly runs between road and river, by Titusville, Lambertville and Stockton. Above Stockton the road swings west along the water, then north for its last miles to Frenchtown.

Lambertville, Stockton and Frenchtown all went by ferry names first. Frenchtown got its name from a Swiss refugee of the French Revolution and his French-speaking neighbors, and the five piers of its first bridge to Pennsylvania, built in 1841, still stand.

moments.title: Washington Crossing State Park
moments.text: The Johnson Ferry House, a farmhouse and tavern, stands near where Washington's 2,400 men came over the river the night of December 25, 1776, on their way to Trenton.

moments.title: Prallsville Mills
moments.text: Where Wickecheoke Creek meets the Delaware, an 1877 grist mill keeps company with a 1790 linseed oil mill, which now holds an artist's studio.

moments.title: Raven Rock
moments.text: From Bulls Island a bridge crosses to Lumberville, Pennsylvania. It carried road traffic from 1856 to 1944 and now carries walkers.
